author: Mymy220AKAMimi
title: This Subscription Is A Scam For Light Users
content:
I rarely print and only need to replace my ink cartridges about once a year. Paying $7.99 per month for HP Instant Ink adds up to $95.88 a year, which is more than it would cost me to simply buy replacement cartridges myself.

I decided to cancel my subscription with 100 pages remaining for the month (and realistically, it should have been more since unused pages from previous months weren’t used at all) and I still have full ink cartridges still installed. After canceling, HP informed me that the Instant Ink cartridges would be disabled, meaning I could no longer use the ink I had already paid for. To print again, I now have to spend about $69 on regular, non-HP InstaInk cartridges.

That is a scam. I paid for the subscription, and the cartridges are still full, yet HP remotely blocks them from working once you cancel. To make matters worse, I couldn’t even remove my credit card information from the app.

If you print a high volume of pages every month, Instant Ink might make sense. But if you’re a light user, you’re likely to spend far more than necessary. You’re better off buying regular cartridges when you actually need them. Because of this experience, I won’t be purchasing HP products ever again.

author: Yellowpantstime
title: A Printing App That Makes Its Own Print Menu Unreadable
content:
This app is astonishingly bad at the one thing it is supposed to do: print.

On an iPhone in Dark Mode, the print-options menu can display white text on a white background, making the controls completely unreadable. That is not a minor cosmetic glitch. It makes the app functionally unusable. The official workaround is apparently to change the appearance setting for the entire phone just to use HP’s app, which is absurd.

HP has had ample time and resources to fix a basic interface defect that should never have passed quality control in the first place. Instead, customers who already paid for HP hardware are left troubleshooting an app that cannot reliably display its own menus.

A printer app should make printing easier. This one adds frustration, wastes time, and reflects an embarrassing lack of attention to basic usability.

author: GreaterPeoriaDude
title: There isn’t really a point to it…
content: The HP Printing App feels like it exists mostly to stand in the doorway and remind you that your printer would love to become a subscription service. Nearly everything it offers is already handled perfectly fine by an iPhone, including finding the printer, selecting a file, and hitting print. Groundbreaking stuff. I downloaded it because I needed one very normal, very useful feature: the ability to adjust an image’s print size. Somehow, amid all the promotional nudges and extra menus, that option is nowhere to be found. Instead, the app adds another layer between me and a task that should take ten seconds. The printer itself gives me just as much useful information, and at least it does not keep trying to sell me on a monthly relationship. It works, technically, but it adds more bloat than value. Two stars for existing and connecting. The rest is mostly vibes, subscriptions, and missed opportunities.

author: Chic by bey
title: Chef
content: I went to Best Buy today and spent a lot of time comparing printers. I scanned almost every printer they had—probably all but three or four. I researched each one carefully, including this model, and it consistently received excellent reviews. I even compared it to several Brother printers, but I ultimately chose the HP Smart Tank because it seemed much easier to use. After setting it up today, I can honestly say I made the right decision. The setup was straightforward, the app is user-friendly, and I’m genuinely excited to use it as I build my business. This printer feels like an investment in my future, and I’m grateful I chose it.

author: MindieKaye
title: WARNING
content: There are so many problems with my HP printers that I don’t even know where to start. My old one refuses to connect anymore, and despite doing every single thing suggested by the AI chatbot and reading the community help forums- which, by the way, are the only options for getting help, as HP does not have a customer service phone number- it still won’t work. So I bought a brand new OfficeJet printer three days ago. Despite easily going through the setup process and getting the “congratulations, your setup is complete!” message. The printer display keeps telling me to go to the app because my setup is not complete. I go to the app- it says setup is complete. When I get lucky and can manage to send a document to print, it only holds it in the print queue because it says it’s a private pickup, even though the private pickup is (and always has been) toggled off. I’ve rebooted, the private pickup is still toggled off, but it will not print because it says it’s a private pickup. Even if it was a private pickup, I was standing right at the printer with location turned on. Still nothing. The AI chatbot “help” just tells me that I need to toggle the private pickup off. IT’S. ALREADY. TOGGLED. OFF. I’ve searched everywhere for a customer service phone number. It doesn’t exist. I give up. The new printer is being returned, and I’ll never buy another HP product again.
